newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs' confidence in government slips -- poll.
newsitem.headline: Czechs' confidence in government slips -- poll.

text.p: Czechs' confidence in their government has slipped to its lowest in more than a year since the three-party coalition last month revealed a package of measures to kick-start the economy, a poll showed on Monday.
Just 35 percent of respondents said they trusted the government, down from 38 percent in April, according to the poll by the IVVM agency. A year ago, 47 percent trusted the government.
Of the 1,001 people polled between April 30 and May 5, 61 percent said they distrusted the government, up from 59 percent in April.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's centre-right administration last month announced a package of measures aimed at giving fresh impetus to economic growth and curbing trade and current account deficits and clamping down on economic crime.
It included cuts in public spending and limits on wage growth.

Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik was chiefly blamed for the country's problems, with 28 percent of those polled saying he should resign, followed by Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy on 22 percent. Eighteen percent said Klaus should go.
Tension has also been growing between coalition partners, with some leading ministers calling for the government to be restructured.
